messages.subject: Trouble shooting data problems for RSF
parts:
Hi Chris, 

During Animove 2024, you mentioned that the rsf.fit would be able to handle choppy data and irregular sampling at different levels. I'm currently having trouble with it because of problematic individuals.

I'm attaching the code I'm using (file called 3. SEO_RSF_multiple.R), and the problem I have is when using akde (line 102 of the code). The logic is that some individuals are not able to have a proper convergence of the model due to the amount of data (or at least that is what I think). 

Upon inspection (using the other code I'm attaching, SEO_diagnostic.R), based on your suggestions online, the variograms do not show good data.

I followed Bjorn's code, which I'm also attaching in case you need the context of what I was trying to do.

The raster files can be downloaded directly from this Google Drive folder.

So, my main question is how to troubleshoot within CTMM to either filter out these individuals or use the poor information these individuals provide. 

Thank you so much for any advice or insight.

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: Trouble shooting data problems for RSF
parts:
Hi Josue,

I can see some issues:
  1. Some of the variograms look like the individual isn't resident during the tracking period. The biggest red flags are PS0026_ASI13 and PS0005_ASI12.
  2. Individual PS0095_ASI12 (and maybe some others) doesn't appear to be moving much at all, and would need a location error model to better resolve (but this is probably just nesting behavior or something?).
  3. Between the largest migratory/dispersal ranges and the smallest nest-bound ranges, there's 6 orders of magnitude difference in range area, so the default grid (largest extent at highest resolution) probably won't work. So even if the data didn't need any cleaning, you would want to specify a coarser resolution or change the resolution calculation (see the help('akde') grid arguments).
Best,
Chris
